To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CPU cost of a streaming join can be modeled as a function of the join selectivity and the number of tuples in the window; that the problem of load shedding under CPU limitations can be reduced to the problem of shedding tuples from a window; that the Probe-No-Insert strategy is a good candidate for random load shedding; and that the CPU cost model and load shedding algorithms proposed in this work are applicable for any streaming join algorithm.

(i) CPU cost can be accurately modeled by the product of the number of CPU cycles and the number of CPU cores; (ii) the problem of finding the maximum possible subset under CPU limitations can be formulated and solved efficiently; (iii) the Probe-No-Insert random load shedding strategy dominates all previously proposed strategies for symmetric hash join.

(i) CPU limited streaming window joins can be approximated with the goal of obtaining a superset of the complete answer and (ii) the previously proposed coin flip random load shedding strategy can be improved.
